Simulate UNO Turn-by-Turn Gameplay

play_turns_loop.Rd

Executes the main gameplay loop of UNO by iterating through player turns until a winner is found. Handles all playable card logic, card draws, action cards (Skip, Reverse, +2), and wild card behavior, including forced draws and color changes.

Usage

play_turns_loop(hands, deck, discard, direction, turn)

Arguments

hands

A named list of tibbles representing each player’s hand. Each tibble must have columns color, value, and type.

deck

A tibble representing the remaining draw pile. Cards are removed from here when players must draw.

discard

A tibble representing the discard pile. The last row is treated as the top card in play.

direction

An integer indicating turn order. 1 for clockwise (default), -1 for counter-clockwise.

turn

Integer. The current player’s turn index (1-based). This is updated automatically within the loop.

Value

A named list with the following components:

  • winner – A character string. Name of the winning player (e.g., "Player_3").

  • hands – A named list of tibbles showing the final hands of all players. Only the winner has zero cards.

  • discard – A tibble representing the final discard pile, including the last played card.

Details

This function is best used internally by play_game or during custom simulations where you want to experiment with specific starting states.

- Handles action cards: "skip", "reverse", "+2", "wild", "wild_draw4"
- If no playable card, player draws 1 from deck
- Turn logic accounts for action card effects (e.g., next player drawing, reversing direction)
- Wilds automatically assign a random color

Examples

# Full setup and simulation step-by-step
state <- setup_game()
#> Error in setup_game(): argument "n_players" is missing, with no default
outcome <- play_turns_loop(
  hands = state$hands,
  deck = state$deck,
  discard = state$discard,
  direction = state$direction,
  turn = state$turn
)
#> Error: object 'state' not found
outcome$winner
#> Error: object 'outcome' not found
